reconcile.note: Fausset notes the clan totals sum to 22,300 and attributes the extra 300 to exempted firstborn Levites, scriptural rounding, or a scribal error.

discrepancy.note: Colenso and Wellhausen both flag the Levite clan totals of Numbers 3 as summing to 22,300 against the chapter's own stated total of 22,000.

quotes.text: numbered separately as Gershonites, 7,500 … the sum of which three numbers, however, is actually 22,300
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. II (1863), on Numbers 3:22 and 3:39.

quotes.text: There are 22,273 firstborn males to be provided for, and there are 22,000 male Levites above a month old. The 273 extra firstborn males are specially redeemed at five shekels a head. What accuracy!
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 trans.), on Numbers 3:39.

sides.snippet: Those who were numbered of them, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, even those who were numbered of them were seven thousand five hundred.
sides.verseText: Those who were numbered of them, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, even those who were numbered of them were seven thousand five hundred.

sides.snippet: All who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
sides.verseText: All who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
